parts.label: whole
parts.technique: Discrete probability distribution with E(X) used to find parameters
parts.reason: The method requires using E(X)=1 to deduce a=c, which is calculation of the mean of a discrete random variable, explicitly excluded by S4.1 ('calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables is excluded'). No alternative in-spec method reaches full marks since the mean calculation is essential.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Venn diagram construction
parts.reason: S3.1/S3.2 guidance explicitly mentions Venn diagrams for probability problems.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Mutually exclusive events
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly covers mutually exclusive events.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Basic probability from Venn diagram
parts.reason: Direct application of S3.1/S3.2 probability calculation.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Testing independence via P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B)
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly gives the independence test formula.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Conditional probability
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers conditional probability calculation.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Conditional probability with union and complement
parts.reason: S3.2 covers conditional probability formula and combination with complement/union rules.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculation of Smp (covariance sum) for correlation/regression
parts.reason: This sum underlies the correlation coefficient/regression formula calculation, which S5.1 and S2.2 explicitly exclude ('use of the formula is not required'/'calculations involving regression lines are excluded').

parts.label: b
parts.technique: PMCC calculation using formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly excludes use of the PMCC formula; only calculator-based values are permitted, but here the mark scheme requires the formula calculation from summary statistics.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Interpreting correlation/scatter diagram
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly covers informal interpretation of correlation and consistency with a scatter diagram, without requiring calculation.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Using totals to find a proportionality constant
parts.reason: Not a regression/correlation calculation; it's basic use of totals/ratio, loosely related to S2.2's proportional relationship guidance, though not explicitly this exact scenario.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Linear regression line equation calculation
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly excludes 'calculations involving regression lines'.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Using regression line to estimate value
parts.reason: Depends directly on the out-of-spec regression equation from (e); also itself a regression-line calculation excluded by S2.2.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: Comparing manager's model and regression model
parts.reason: This relies on values computed from the excluded regression model in (e)/(f), so it only makes sense after an out-of-spec part.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Histogram bar width/height (frequency density)
parts.reason: S2.1 explicitly covers histograms and area representing frequency.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Linear interpolation for quartile from grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly states 'use of linear interpolation to calculate percentiles from grouped data is expected'.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Describing skewness from quartiles
parts.reason: No statement mentions 'skewness' anywhere in the specification; S2.3/S2.4 discuss central tendency and variation but not skewness as a named concept, so this named concept is not covered.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Mean and standard deviation from summary statistics/grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculating standard deviation, including from summary statistics, for grouped/continuous data.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Skewness coefficient formula
parts.reason: Skewness is not mentioned by any specification statement, so this named concept and its formula are out of spec.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Effect of regrouping data on estimates of median and mean
parts.reason: This is a reasoning/interpretation task about linear interpolation and grouped data estimates, which extends S2.3's coverage of grouped data and central tendency measures.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability via standardisation
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding value from symmetric normal interval probability
parts.reason: S4.2 covers use of Normal distribution and standardisation to solve for unknown parameters; questions may involve solving equations.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Normal distribution combined with quadratic inequality for rectangle area
parts.reason: Combines S4.2 Normal probability calculation with P2.5 quadratic inequality solving, both in spec; no excluded content (no pdf, no CLT).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sum of discrete probability distribution equals 1
parts.reason: S4.1 covers discrete probability distributions; summing probabilities to 1 is not the excluded mean/variance calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating E(S) of a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables'.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Expected profit calculation using E(S) type reasoning
parts.reason: This requires computing an expectation (260×P(S=5)-10 is essentially E of a transformed discrete rv), which is excluded per S4.1's exclusion of mean calculation for discrete random variables.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Explaining a probability using independent trial reasoning
parts.reason: This is basic probability reasoning (product of probabilities for sequential independent-type events), covered by S3.1/S4.1 without needing mean/variance.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Constructing a discrete probability distribution in terms of p
parts.reason: S4.1 covers understanding and using discrete probability distributions as a model; no mean/variance calculation required here.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Solving for p using expected profit comparison
parts.reason: Requires E(profit) computation (mean of a discrete random variable), excluded by S4.1, and depends on the out-of-spec expected profit from (c).
